hero.description: Houston is the most ethnically diverse large city in the USA, and its soccer culture runs as deep as any in North America. NRG Stadium hosts the World Cup in a city where Latin American, African, Asian, and Caribbean communities have built one of the most authentic football fan cultures on the continent. Expect the most passionate crowd of any tournament venue.

stadium.name: NRG Stadium
stadium.transport: NRG Stadium is in the NRG Park complex, about 8 km south of downtown. The METRORail Red Line has an NRG Park stop — about 15 minutes from downtown Main St stops. Rideshare and game-day shuttles are also used. The Red Line is strongly preferred on match days.

quick_facts.matches_hosted: Multiple matches including group stage and advanced rounds
quick_facts.fan_hub_status: Fan hub expected at Discovery Green; confirm local schedules

weather.june: Very hot and humid, highs 32–35°C (90–95°F). Afternoon thunderstorms are common. This is peak Houston summer.
weather.july: Hottest and most humid month. Highs 33–37°C (91–99°F). NRG Stadium's retractable roof means match conditions are controlled.
packing_tips: Lightweight, moisture-wicking clothing is essential — Houston humidity is intense
A compact umbrella or rain layer for afternoon storms
Sunscreen and a hat for outdoor fan zones — the sun is aggressive even with cloud cover
Carry a large water bottle — dehydration in Houston summer heat happens fast

airports.name: George Bush Intercontinental Airport
airports.distance_to_stadium: About 40 km north of NRG Stadium
transfer_options: IAH to Downtown Houston via METRORail Red Line extension — about 50 min (check schedule for airport service)
Rideshare from IAH to Downtown hotels takes 35–50 minutes depending on traffic
Taxi stand available at the ground transportation level
airports.notes: Main international hub. Rideshare or taxi is the most practical option for arriving international visitors. Bush Intercontinental is the best airport for direct international flights.

airports.name: William P. Hobby Airport
transfer_options: METRORail Red Line: Hobby Airport connection — about 20 min to NRG Park
Rideshare from Hobby to Downtown or NRG Stadium — 20–30 min
airports.notes: Closer to the stadium than Bush Intercontinental. Good for Southwest Airlines passengers and fans staying near the stadium or Museum District.

match_schedule.teams_or_placeholder: NRG Stadium hosts multiple matches. Full schedule after group draw.

public_transit: METRORail Red Line: NRG Park station — direct service from Downtown and Midtown
Red Line connects to Hobby Airport (HOU) as well as Downtown Main St corridor
Extra rail service on match days — confirm schedule on the METRO website
rideshare: Rideshare is practical pre-match but post-match surge from NRG is severe
Walk along Kirby Dr away from the stadium for a faster post-match pickup
Pre-book a scheduled Uber or Lyft before kickoff to lock pricing
driving_parking: NRG Park has extensive parking — NRG lots are closest to the stadium gate
Main St and Loop 610 back up severely after full-capacity events
Park-and-ride with the METRO Red Line from further north is a practical alternative
walking_biking: Museum District and Medical Center neighbourhoods are walking distance from NRG Park
Not walkable from Downtown — 6+ km in dangerous summer heat
B-Cycle bikeshare exists in limited areas of Houston
match_day_tips: NRG Stadium has a retractable roof — match conditions are controlled regardless of the extreme weather outside
Hydrate before entering the stadium — Houston heat drains you fast in the outdoor queues
Museum District restaurants and bars are within walking distance for pre-match
Arrive at least 90 minutes early — NRG Park draws huge crowds and queues are long

fan_hubs.name: Houston Fan Hub — Discovery Green
fan_hubs.description: A major fan hub expected at Discovery Green — Houston's downtown park designed for large outdoor events. Giant screens, food trucks from Houston's world-class restaurant scene, live entertainment, and the proximity of the George R. Brown Convention Center make this a natural epicentre.
transport_tips: METRORail Red Line to Main St/Discovery Green area
Walking distance from many Downtown hotels
Multiple bus routes serve the Discovery Green area

neighborhoods.name: Downtown
neighborhoods.best_for: Hotels, fan hub access, Metro connections
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe in the main business and hotel corridors. Discovery Green area is busy and well-patrolled.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: METRORail Red Line south to NRG Park — 15 min
neighborhoods.description: Largest concentration of business hotels and the expected Discovery Green fan hub. Easy Metro access to NRG Stadium. Downtown Houston has improved significantly and is quite walkable within the core.

neighborhoods.name: Midtown
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Active and safe along Main St and Midtown corridors.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: METRORail Red Line from Midtown stops — about 10 min to NRG
neighborhoods.description: Young, lively neighbourhood on the Red Line corridor. Excellent bar and restaurant scene, walkable stretches, and an active local soccer bar culture.

neighborhoods.name: Montrose
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Safe, eclectic neighbourhood with active street life.
neighborhoods.stadium_access: Bus or rideshare to NRG — about 20 min
neighborhoods.description: Houston's most culturally diverse neighbourhood. The best independent restaurants, bars, and galleries in the city. Slightly removed from the Metro but full of character.

neighborhoods.name: EaDo (East Downtown)
neighborhoods.best_for: Soccer culture, nightlife, PNC Stadium proximity
neighborhoods.safety_transit_notes: Gentrifying area — active in the bar/restaurant zone, quieter away from it.
neighborhoods.description: Houston's emerging arts and nightlife district adjacent to Downtown. Home to PNC Stadium (Houston Dynamo) and some of the best soccer bars in the city.

hotels.name: Marriott Marquis Houston
hotels.distance: 15 min to NRG Stadium via Red Line
hotels.best_for: Luxury, rooftop pool, Discovery Green proximity

hotels.name: Hotel Alessandra
hotels.distance: 15 min to stadium via Red Line

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency Houston
hotels.best_for: Large groups, central Downtown, convention access

bars.name: Pitch 25
bars.notes: Houston's best dedicated soccer bar adjacent to PNC Stadium. Watch parties here are absolutely electric.

bars.name: Black Labrador Pub
bars.notes: British-style pub in Montrose with strong soccer culture and reliable match showings.

bars.name: Axelrad Beer Garden
bars.notes: Tropical outdoor beer garden in Midtown — great afternoon match vibe with hammocks and food trucks.

bars.name: The Rustic Houston
bars.notes: Large outdoor venue with live music and screens. Good for post-match gatherings.

bars.name: Houston Social
bars.notes: Neighbourhood sports bar with a loyal soccer-watching crowd. Shows early morning European matches.

transport.summary: Houston is spread out and car-dependent, but the METRORail Red Line provides reliable access from Downtown and Midtown directly to NRG Stadium. It's the clear best option on match days.
tips: METRO Q Card: tap-to-pay on METRORail — load at any station kiosk
Red Line from Main Street Square to NRG Park station — 15 minutes, much better than driving
Hobby Airport (HOU) has Red Line connections — very convenient compared to IAH
Houston heat is dangerous in outdoor queues — the stadium roof controls conditions inside
Rideshare is essential for non-Rail areas like Montrose, EaDo, and Museum District

fan_zones.name: Houston Fan Hub — Discovery Green
fan_zones.description: Downtown Houston's premier outdoor event space — expected fan hub with giant screens, food trucks, and live entertainment throughout the tournament.

soccer_culture.community_notes: Houston has one of the most passionate soccer communities in the USA. The city's enormous Mexican, Central American, Colombian, Nigerian, Vietnamese, and other immigrant communities all bring deep football cultures. Houston Dynamo's PNC Stadium hosts some of the loudest crowds in MLS. This is the real deal.
historic_venues: PNC Stadium (Houston Dynamo home, formerly BBVA Stadium)

tourist_hits.name: Space Center Houston
tourist_hits.notes: NASA's visitor complex — interactive exhibits, mission control tours, and real spacecraft. Book in advance.

tourist_hits.name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
tourist_hits.notes: Gem and mineral collection, dinosaur halls, and excellent rotating exhibitions.

tourist_hits.name: Museum of Fine Arts Houston
tourist_hits.notes: One of the largest art museums in the USA — free on Thursdays.

tourist_hits.name: Houston Zoo
tourist_hits.notes: Large, well-maintained zoo in Hermann Park adjacent to the Museum District.

local_favorites.name: Buffalo Bayou Park
local_favorites.notes: 5 km riverside park with cycling, kayaking, and outdoor art. Beautiful in the cooler morning hours.

local_favorites.name: Kemah Boardwalk
local_favorites.notes: Waterfront entertainment district 45 min from Downtown — rides, seafood restaurants, and bay views.

local_favorites.name: Chinatown / Bellaire Blvd
local_favorites.notes: One of the best Chinese, Vietnamese, and pan-Asian restaurant areas in the USA.

areas: Montrose — independent restaurants and bars, the most eclectic neighbourhood
Midtown — active bar strip along Main St and Milam
EaDo — soccer bar culture and emerging restaurant scene
Chinatown / Bellaire Blvd — authentic pan-Asian food

recommendations.name: Uchi Houston
recommendations.notes: James Beard-winning Japanese restaurant from Tyson Cole. Book well ahead.

recommendations.name: Underbelly Hospitality
recommendations.notes: Chris Shepherd's Houston-centric restaurant group — excellent for the city's food story.

recommendations.name: Teotihuacan Mexican Cafe
recommendations.notes: The best authentic Mexican food in Houston — multiple locations, cash-friendly.

local_resources.emergency_info: Emergency: 911. Houston Police non-emergency: (713) 884-3131. Hospital: Houston Methodist Hospital, (713) 790-3311.

walk_bike.walkability_summary: Houston is not a pedestrian city overall, but Downtown, Midtown along Main St, and Montrose have walkable corridors. Bayou Greenway trails offer excellent cycling routes.
walk_bike.bikeability_summary: BCycle Houston operates bikeshare in Downtown, Midtown, and Montrose. Bayou Greenway provides car-free cycling routes.
walk_bike.bike_share_notes: BCycle Houston docks in Downtown, Midtown, and EaDo. Day passes in the BCycle app. Buffalo Bayou and Bayou Greenway are the best cycling routes.

pickup_soccer.name: Burnett Bayland Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: One of Houston's most active informal soccer parks with Hispanic community pickup culture.

pickup_soccer.name: MacGregor Park
pickup_soccer.access_notes: South Houston park with strong Latino soccer culture and multiple fields.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Galveston Island
outdoors_day_trips.notes: Gulf of Mexico beach island with a historic Strand District. Good for a full day between matches.

outdoors_day_trips.name: Big Thicket National Preserve
outdoors_day_trips.notes: A biological crossroads of North America — hiking trails through remarkable forest diversity.

safety_tips: Houston is safe in tourist areas — Downtown, Midtown, Montrose, Museum District
Use rideshare or the Metro for late-night travel — avoid walking in unfamiliar areas
Houston heat in June–July can be dangerous — hydrate constantly and take indoor breaks during peak afternoon heat
The NRG Stadium retractable roof controls match conditions — pack a layer for air-conditioned interiors
Lock valuables in your hotel safe — car break-ins do occur in parking areas
